title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 706
text:
31. Although it is generally necessary for everyone to mute themselves when not speaking to
avoid background noise, be aware that this means the judge cannot hear the normal
feedback people give to each other to indicate they are listening. It will be harder for a judge
to know when a party is disengaged.

32. It is always important with LIPs to ensure they do not feel excluded by legal or procedural
discussions between the judge and the representative on the other side. This is even more
important with a remote hearing where they may feel their presence is scarcely noticed. It
may help to regularly come to them first for comments, having explained to the other side
why this is being done.

33. LIPs may easily get left behind when documents are referred to. Check at the outset whether
they have an electronic or hard copy of the bundle. Either way, the judge will not be able to
see if they have not found the page, so check each time that they have done so before any
representative on the other side rushes on with questions or representations.
